title: Coherent comparison data for Cartesian postcomposition squares
statement: Use small quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces and spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], postcomposition by an edge from [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], coherent realization and locally Kan replacement from [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and coherent Hom bifunctors and composition from [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], with the simultaneous twisted-arrow normalization of [lem-cbc-hom-functor-composition-coherence]. Let $p:E\to B$ be any simplicial map between small quasicategories, let $e:b\to c$ be an edge of $E$, and let $a$ be a vertex of $E$. Put $D_S=\mathfrak C[S]$ and choose the functorial object-preserving locally Kan replacements $r_S:D_S\to R D_S$ for $S=E,B$, with induced simplicial functor $R p:R D_E\to R D_B$; put $W_S=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R D_S)$, let $\alpha_S:S\to W_S$ be adjoint to $r_S$, and let $W_p=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(Rp)$, so that $W_p\alpha_E=\alpha_Bp$. Consider three squares, each with corners indexed by $(E;a,b),(E;a,c),(B;pa,pb),(B;pa,pc)$: (i) the right-pinched square $\operatorname{Map}_E(a,b)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(a,c)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_B(pa,pb)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(pa,pc)$, with vertical maps induced by $p$ and horizontal maps representatives of the second-variable Hom action, namely postcomposition by $e$ and $p(e)$; (ii) the same square in $W_E,W_B$, with vertical maps induced by $W_p$ and horizontal maps representatives of postcomposition by $\alpha_E(e)$ and $\alpha_B(pe)$; (iii) the strictly commuting enriched square $RD_E(a,b)\to RD_E(a,c)$ over $RD_B(pa,pb)\to RD_B(pa,pc)$, with vertical maps induced by $Rp$ and horizontal maps enriched composition with $r_E([e])$ and $r_B([pe])$. Choose the Hom data in this finite functor diagram with the normalization just specified. Square (i) carries the canonical naturality homotopy of $p_*$ at $(\mathrm{id}_a,e)$ and square (ii) carries that of $(W_p)_*$ at $(\mathrm{id}_a,\alpha_E(e))$; these are the specified commutation homotopies, the commutation homotopy of (iii) is constant, and there are comparisons (i)$\to$(ii), whose corner maps are induced by $\alpha_E,\alpha_B$, and (iii)$\to$(ii), whose corner maps are the natural coherent-nerve comparisons $RD_S(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{W_S}(x,y)$ (represented by maps of Kan complexes chosen from the natural equivalence of coherent Hom diagrams). Every corner map is a weak homotopy equivalence, and each comparison carries the following coherent-cube data. Write a comparison as source square $(f,g,u,v;H)$, with $f:A\to U$, $g:A\to V$, $u:U\to Z$, $v:V\to Z$ and $H:uf\simeq vg$, target square $(f',g',u',v';H')$, and corner maps $\bar a:A\to A'$, $\bar b:U\to U'$, $\bar c:V\to V'$, $\bar d:Z\to Z'$. There are specified simplicial homotopies $L:\bar bf\simeq f'\bar a$, $M:\bar cg\simeq g'\bar a$, $N:\bar du\simeq u'\bar b$, $O:\bar dv\simeq v'\bar c$ and a homotopy relative endpoints between the two boundary paths $$\bar d uf\xrightarrow{\bar dH}\bar d vg\xrightarrow{Og}v'\bar c g\xrightarrow{v'M}v'g'\bar a,\qquad \bar d uf\xrightarrow{Nf}u'\bar b f\xrightarrow{u'L}u'f'\bar a\xrightarrow{H'\bar a}v'g'\bar a,$$ the paths being represented after Kan fillers. The homotopies and the boundary-path homotopy are chosen together by restricting the indicated coherent Hom comparisons to this fixed finite diagram. This statement asserts comparison and coherence data only; it asserts no homotopy-pullback property.

source.place: Proposition 8.3.3.2 (03N2), Corollary 8.3.5.8 (046J), Remark 8.3.5.9 (03PD), together with HTT Theorem 2.2.5.1. The displayed boundary-path formulation is the explicit square restriction of the coherent Hom naturality and is an agent expansion; archival copies WANTED.

proof.text: Set $D_S=\mathfrak C[S]$ and use the object-preserving functorial replacement of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The adjuncts $\alpha_S:S\to W_S$ satisfy $W_p\alpha_E=\alpha_Bp$: on each simplex both adjoints are given by the same enriched functor, because $Rp\,r_E=r_B\mathfrak C[p]$. Use the right-pinched convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Choose Hom actions and induced transformations simultaneously for the finite strict diagram with objects $E,B,W_E,W_B$, including their equal composites, by [lem-cbc-hom-functor-composition-coherence]. By [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] the second-variable actions are postcomposition, so they give the horizontal representatives in (i) and (ii). Denote their naturality homotopies by $h_T$ for each functor $T$ in the diagram. Thus set $H=h_p(e)$ in (i) and $H'=h_{W_p}(\alpha_Ee)$ in (ii); these choices fix the commutation data before comparing squares.

For (i)$\to$(ii) take the four actual corner maps induced by $\alpha_E,\alpha_B$. Set $L=h_{\alpha_E}(e)$ and $O=h_{\alpha_B}(pe)$. The equalities $\alpha_Bp=W_p\alpha_E$ induce equal maps on right-pinched simplices, so take $M,N$ constant. Apply [lem-cbc-hom-functor-composition-coherence] to $(p,\alpha_B)$ and to $(\alpha_E,W_p)$. The resulting paths are respectively
$$\alpha_B h_p(e)\;\cdot\;h_{\alpha_B}(pe)\,p,\qquad W_p h_{\alpha_E}(e)\;\cdot\;h_{W_p}(\alpha_Ee)\,\alpha_E.$$
Both are homotopic relative endpoints to $h_{\alpha_Bp}(e)=h_{W_p\alpha_E}(e)$. Reverse one of these relative homotopies and concatenate to obtain a relative-endpoint homotopy between the displayed paths. With $M,N$ constant, these are exactly the two boundary paths in the statement. This uses composition compatibility of transformations, not merely naturality in the object variables of a single transformation.

source.place: Corollary 8.3.5.8, together with the composition-normalized refinement isolated in lem-cbc-hom-functor-composition-coherence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-rigidification-postcomposition-comparison] separately to $S=E$ and $S=B$. Its hypotheses are precisely that these are small quasicategories and $r_S:\mathfrak C[S]\to R\mathfrak C[S]$ is an object-preserving locally Kan replacement, which Step 1 supplied. Its first conclusion says that the actual maps of right-pinched mapping spaces induced by $\alpha_S$ are weak homotopy equivalences, for every pair of vertices. Consequently all four corner maps in (i)$\to$(ii) have the required property. This conclusion is taken from this node, rather than inferred from the replacement clause of the coherent-nerve theorem alone.

Put $A=RD_E$, $C=RD_B$, $F=Rp$. Write $K_A:A^{\mathrm{op}}\times A\to\operatorname{Kan}$ for the enriched Hom functor. It sends a pair of morphisms $(u,v)$ to $t\mapsto vtu$. The enriched maps $F_{x,y}$ give a transformation $K_A\to K_C(F^{\mathrm{op}}\times F)$, since $F(vtu)=F(v)F(t)F(u)$ is an equality of simplicial maps. Restricting to $u=1_a$, $v=r_E[e]$ gives square (iii), including its constant commutation homotopy; naturality of $r$ identifies $F(r_E[e])=r_B[pe]$.

By [lem-coef-enriched-hom-twisted-arrow-comparison], the coherent nerve of $K_A$ classifies the twisted-arrow coupling of $W_E$, with its comparison natural for simplicial functors and respecting higher pre/postcomposition. The same holds for $C$. Apply the full mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] to these equivalences of left fibrations and to the map induced by $F$. Its compatibility with composition and base pullback identifies the enriched transformation just written with the normalized $(W_p)_*$, together with the comparison between them as transformations. In particular this is a comparison in the arrow functor category: it includes compatibility with $(W_p)_*$, not only objectwise weak equivalences. Restrict it along $(\mathrm{id}_a,\alpha_Ee)$ to obtain an equivalence of square diagrams from (iii) to (ii). Its target square has exactly $H'=h_{W_p}(\alpha_Ee)$, because both transformations use the twisted-arrow normalization fixed in Step 1.

source.place: Construction 8.3.6.1 (03N6), Proposition 8.3.6.2 (03N7); twisted-arrow classification and its composition-compatible mapping-space comparison.

proof.text:
Take the components of the coherent equivalence of square diagrams in Step 4 as the four corner maps $\beta_{S,x,y}:RD_S(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}_{W_S}(x,y)$. These are the coherent-nerve mapping comparisons: this identification on fibers, including the identity point, is part of [lem-coef-enriched-hom-twisted-arrow-comparison]. Each is a weak equivalence by the mapping-space conclusion of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Choose this direct-map representation, so no intermediate square of an unspecified zigzag is needed.

Here is the explicit extraction of the coherence datum. A coherent transformation between square diagrams is a diagram on $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$. Its bottom and top square faces are the constant homotopy of (iii) and the prescribed $H'$; its four side faces give $L,M,N,O$. By [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces] its simplices are enriched functors to Kan complexes. Subdivide the cube into the six tetrahedra indexed by the orders of its three coordinates. The tetrahedra identify successive ways of pasting adjacent square faces; their common triangular faces are equal restrictions. Pasting them identifies the boundary path through $\bar dH,Og,v'M$ with that through $Nf,u'L,H'\bar a$, fixing the common first and last maps. In $\operatorname{Fun}(A,Z')$, which is Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan], choose fillers to represent these path concatenations and the relative-endpoint homotopy. These fillers represent the coherent cube already constructed; no equality of component classes is being used to assert the cube's existence.

source.place: Agent expansion of the auxiliary Cartesian mapping-square interface: restriction of a coherent comparison to a square and its prism.

proof.text: Steps 1--3 give (i)$\to$(ii) with the required four weak equivalences, four side homotopies and relative-endpoint boundary homotopy. Steps 4--5 give the same data for (iii)$\to$(ii), with its strict source square carrying the constant homotopy. Hence both comparisons have precisely the data asserted in the statement. The hypotheses used were only smallness and the quasicategory condition for $E,B$; no inner-fibration or Cartesian-edge hypothesis was introduced. The construction concerns this finite diagram and does not assert an additional undefined naturality in the parameter $p$.
